data.title: Why is Alphabet stock sliding today? By Investing.com
data.summary: Investing.com -- Shares of Alphabet fell 4.2% in morning trading after Malaysia’s communications regulator filed two lawsuits against Google today seeking combined damages of roughly $146 million, alleging the company failed to adequately address harmful content — including online gambling, scams, and fraud — on its YouTube platform. The legal action compounds an already difficult backdrop for the stock, which has been under sustained pressure since a disappointing third-quarter earnings report [...] Adding to the pressure, an unconfirmed supply-chain report suggesting Google could reduce its 2027 orders for custom AI chips (TPU-8i) by roughly 20% has unsettled investors focused on the company’s AI capital allocation strategy. A securities class action lawsuit — with a lead-plaintiff deadline of December 1 — alleging Alphabet misled investors about the timing of its Gemini 3.5 Pro launch also continues to weigh on sentiment, as does a report that Google cancelled a publisher funding deal, [...] The combination of fresh regulatory risk, unresolved legal proceedings, AI chip order uncertainty, and a hostile macro environment pushed Alphabet to trade at its lowest level in over a year, touching a new 52-week low of $262.73 intraday — underscoring how multiple converging headwinds have eroded investor confidence in the stock well beyond the sector-wide selloff. data.title: Shareholders Sue Alphabet (GOOGL) Over Gemini Chatbot Claims - TipRanks.com
data.summary: On July 16, 2026, Alphabet’s Class A common stock fell $16.46 to close at $354.46 per share, and its Class C common stock fell $16.39 to close at $353.58 per share, after Bloomberg reported that Google was months behind schedule on delivering Gemini 3.5 Pro. The Class A share price is down nearly 30% in the last 6 months. The deadline to file for lead plaintiff in this securities lawsuit is December 1, 2026. Is GOOGL a Good Stock to Buy Now? [...] The complaint centers on Alphabet’s public representations about the timeline and progress of its flagship artificial intelligence model, Gemini 3.5 Pro. The class period begins on May 19, 2026, when Alphabet hosted its annual Google I/O developer conference. During the conference, Chief Executive Officer Sundar Pichai announced that Gemini 3.5 Pro would arrive in June 2026, telling attendees to “Give us until next month to get it to you” and describing the chatbot as “showing great [...] According to the complaint, the company reinforced this timeline on June 3, 2026, during a Special Investor Call to discuss AI-driven growth, infrastructure investment, and strategic focus areas. On that call, Pichai stated that “Gemini 3.5 Flash is now available, and we expect Gemini 3.5 Pro will be coming in June.”
